title: Asset Gatekeeper and Performance Synthesis Pipeline
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end gatekeeper pipeline that accepts upstream open-source weight bundles, sanitizes and normalizes formats, runs deterministic conversion to Redwood runtime artifacts, executes a prioritized smoke+canary battery, synthesizes a performance profile, and publishes a pin recommendation to the model catalog with an audit trail.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: weight format detection (HF/ggml/torchstate), manifest validation, license check lighting, deterministic conversion runs, tokenization sanity, forward-pass smoke tests, end-to-end latency/throughput microbenchmarks on standardized hardware slots, basic quality evals (perplexity, sample prompts), performance profile generation (latency P50/P95, memory footprint, throughput curves), pin recommendation logic, automatic draft publishing to the catalog behind a manual approval gate.
- Out-of-scope: full security vetting or compliance certifications (handled by Security team), long-running expensive eval suites (will be scheduled by separate pipeline), change to user-facing catalog UI (product will own approval UX).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Pipeline accepts a compressed artifact and returns a deterministic converted runtime artifact (.rmdl) with conversion metadata and conversion_hash.
2) Smoke suite: tokenization match, 1-step forward pass with ref hash, small sample generation consistent with seed.
3) Profile: latency P50/P95 on 8/16/32 token sequences, peak GPU memory, estimated cost-per-token (using current cost model).
4) Canary gating: if latency P95 or failure rate crosses thresholds, flag for manual review and do not publish pin.
5) Published profile appears in the model catalog as a draft with version pin suggestion and linked conversion artifact, plus audit log entry and required approvers.

Design decisions taken so far:
- Conversion is deterministic: tooling will pin converter version and base docker image, run in hermetic sandbox, and capture the conversion manifest (artifact checksums, torch->fused ops map).
- We will centralize telemetry schema: standardized fields (model_key, converter_version, hw_profile, seq_len, batch_size, p50, p95, failure_rate, mem_peak_bytes). This enables downstream Optimize recommendations.
- Canary gating thresholds initially conservative: p95 increase >30% vs baseline OR failure_rate >1% triggers human review. Baseline comes from the nearby model family if available, else from our synthetic baseline.
- For public OSS models lacking license clarity, the pipeline tags artifact as 'license-review-required' and sets customer_impact to 'low' until Legal clears it.

Risks and mitigations:
- Non-deterministic conversions across environments: mitigate by containerized conversion, pinned libs, and checksum verification step.
- Malformed or malicious weight files: run conversion in isolated K8s namespace with network egress disabled and a time/memory budget.
- Over-publishing bad pins: require at least one approver from Onboarding+PM before final publish; keep draft flow.

Next milestones:
- Finish converter integration and deterministic hashing (owner Rohan) — target 2025-08-18.
- Implement smoke battery and telemetry emitter — target 2025-08-25.
- Automatic draft publish to catalog + webhook for approvers — target 2025-09-05.

Operational notes:
- Every run writes a run_manifest to S3 with: submitted_manifest.json, converter_log.txt, smoke_results.json, profile.json, artifact_checksums.txt, and run_exit_code.
- Canary runs must be flagged in the catalog UI (product) and a Slack webhook posted to #onboarding-notifications with run summary.

Open questions:
- Do we allow automatic pin acceptance (no human) for community models under certain confidence bands? (Triage: likely 'no' for initial rollout.)
- Relationship with Dedicated: should Dedicated customers get pinned variants by default when a new model family is onboarded? (Product to decide.)

Long-term improvements (future tickets):
- Integrate safety signatures and provenance scanning into pre-accept gate.
- Add dataset-driven evals to grade generation quality across prompt suites.
- Generate multi-GPU scaling profiles and batch-aware throughput curves.
comments: 2025-08-11 — Rohan: Initial spike completed for HF->.rmdl converter. Deterministic seed + pinned container reduces hash variance. Found edge case: legacy 'weights.pt' with nonstandard state dict naming causing tokenizer mismatch; added aliasing rules.
2025-08-14 — Ava (PM): Reviewed smoke battery. Requested adding a privacy check step to ensure no obvious PII baked into sample outputs. Security owner assigned follow-up.

2025-08-18 — Rohan: Conversion infra wired into sandboxed job runner. First full conversion ended with non-zero exit on 1 of 62 community artifacts; root cause was a missing fused op in runtime. Marked as dependency for compiler team (ENG-33121).
2025-08-22 — Design review: added canary dashboard mockups and explicit approver list. Design asked for a short summary paragraph per run to surface key regressions to PMs.

2025-08-28 — Telemetry: Canonical schema landed in repo (catalog/telemetry-schema.md). Pushed change to emit p50/p95 and mem_peak_bytes. Also added estimated cost-per-token using current runner rates.
2025-09-01 — Engineering review: added manual approval gate requirement for any model with license flag or delta > 25% on p95. Draft catalog publishing implemented behind feature-flag.

2025-09-02 — QA: smoke tests now include deterministic generation check, tokenizer roundtrip, and a forward-only memory monitor. One flaky case remaining on 16-token throughput test under low-memory host — investigating.
